name: Chicken Adobo
description: Classic Filipino chicken braised in soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, and bay leaves.
rawIngredients: 2 lbs chicken, cut into serving pieces
instructions: Crush the garlic using a mortar and pestle.
Combine chicken, soy sauce, and crushed garlic in a bowl; mix well and marinate for at least 1 hour.
Separate the chicken from the garlic and marinade; set aside.
Heat a pot and add 3 tablespoons of cooking oil.
Pan-fry the marinated chicken for 2 minutes per side, then remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the pot and saute the reserved garlic until it starts to brown.
Return the chicken to the pot.
Add the remaining marinade, peppercorns, and bay leaves.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer for 30 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Add the vinegar, let it boil without stirring, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Add sugar and salt to taste; stir and remove from heat.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve hot with rice.

name: Chicken Tinola
description: Warm ginger-garlic chicken soup with green papaya and malunggay leaves.
rawIngredients: 3 lbs chicken, cut into serving pieces
instructions: Heat cooking oil in a pot. Saute garlic, onion, and ginger until the onion softens.
Add chicken and saute for 2 minutes until light brown.
Pour in the fish sauce and stir.
Add rice wash and bring to a boil. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add water as needed and return to a boil.
Add green papaya wedges and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes until tender.
Season with ground black pepper.
Turn off the heat and add the hot pepper leaves and malunggay leaves. Cover for 2 minutes.
Transfer to a serving bowl and serve.

name: Pork Menudo
description: Hearty pork stew with liver, potatoes, carrots, and hotdogs in tomato sauce.
instructions: Combine pork, soy sauce, and lemon; marinate for at least 1 hour.
Heat oil in a pan and saute garlic and onion until softened.
Add marinated pork and cook for 5 to 7 minutes until lightly browned.
Pour in tomato sauce and water; add bay leaves.
Bring to a boil, then lower heat and simmer for 30 minutes to 1 hour, adding water as needed.
Add liver and hotdogs; cook for 5 minutes.
Add potatoes, carrots, sugar, salt, and pepper; stir and cook for 8 to 12 minutes.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve with warm rice.

name: Beef Caldereta
description: Rich beef stew simmered in tomato sauce with potatoes, carrots, and bell peppers.
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and fry the carrots for 2 minutes, then remove and set aside.
Fry the potatoes until the outer part turns light brown, then remove and set aside.
Using the remaining oil, saute garlic, onion, and thyme until the onion caramelizes.
Add beef short ribs and cook until the outer part turns light brown.
Pour in tomato sauce and red wine, then add soy sauce and water.
Cover the pot and cook on low heat until the beef is completely tender.
Add liver spread and bell peppers; cook for 3 minutes.
Add carrots and potatoes; cook for 3 minutes.
Add olives and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve.

name: Pinakbet Tagalog
description: Mixed native vegetables sauteed with pork and shrimp paste, a Filipino everyday classic.
instructions: Heat cooking oil in a pot; saute onion and garlic until softened, then add ginger.
Add half the lechon kawali and saute for 1 minute.
Pour in water and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes over medium heat.
Add tomato and bagoong alamang; stir, cover, and cook for 3 minutes.
Add kalabasa and kamote; cook for 7 minutes.
Add sitaw, okra, ampalaya, and eggplant; stir, cover, and cook for 5 minutes.
Season with black pepper and add the remaining lechon kawali; cook for 1 minute.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve.

name: Bicol Express
description: Spicy pork belly simmered in coconut milk with shrimp paste and chili peppers.
rawIngredients: 2 lbs pork belly, sliced into strips
instructions: Combine pork, ginger, garlic, onion, Thai chili pepper, Serrano pepper, shrimp paste, and coconut milk in a pan. Mix well, cover, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 50 minutes, stirring occasionally and adding water as needed.
Add the remaining coconut cream and additional shrimp paste if desired.
Continue cooking on low heat until the sauce thickens.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve with warm rice.

name: Kare-Kare
description: Oxtail and vegetables simmered in a rich peanut sauce, served with shrimp paste.
rawIngredients: 1 bundle string beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Boil water in a large pot; add oxtail and onions, simmering for 2.5 to 3 hours until tender.
Add ground peanuts, peanut butter, and the annatto-soaked water; simmer for 5 to 7 minutes.
Stir in the toasted ground rice and simmer for 5 additional minutes.
In a separate pan, saute garlic, then cook the banana flower, eggplant, and string beans for 5 minutes.
Transfer the sauteed vegetables to the main pot.
Add the pechay and season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot with steamed rice and shrimp paste on the side.

name: Sisig
description: Sizzling chopped pork and chicken liver seasoned with onions and mayonnaise.
instructions: Boil water in a pot; add pork belly and pig face. Cover and boil for 1 hour on medium heat. Drain and cool.
Grill the boiled meats for 5 minutes per side, then chop into small pieces.
Heat oil in a pan; saute onion for 1 minute.
Add chicken liver; saute until cooked through, mashing while cooking.
Add the minced meat and chicharon; stir until evenly distributed.
Add chili flakes, onion powder, and black pepper.
Pour in the liquid seasoning; stir.
Add mayonnaise; stir and cook for 3 minutes.
Heat a metal plate with butter; transfer the sisig and cook until sizzling.
Serve with calamansi or lime and white rice.

name: Nilagang Baka
description: Comforting boiled beef soup with potatoes, saba bananas, and leafy greens.
instructions: Combine water and beef broth in a large pot; bring to a boil.
Add onion, star anise, and celery; reduce heat to medium, cover, and boil for 20 minutes.
Remove the aromatics using a strainer or skimmer; discard.
Add beef and simmer for 60 to 90 minutes until tender, adding water as needed.
Add saba bananas and potatoes; cook for 10 minutes.
Add bok choy and cabbage; season with salt and pepper.
Cover the pot with heat off; let the vegetables cook for 2 to 5 minutes.
Transfer to a serving bowl and serve.

name: Pancit Canton
description: Stir-fried flour noodles with pork, shrimp, and vegetables, a Filipino party staple.
instructions: Blanch the snap peas, carrots, and cabbage for 35 to 50 seconds, then transfer to an ice bath and drain.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Saute onion and garlic until fragrant and softened.
Add pork and sausage; cook for 2 minutes until lightly browned.
Pour in soy sauce and oyster sauce; stir to coat.
Add chicken broth and water; season with salt and pepper.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 5 to 10 minutes until the pork is tender.
Add shrimp and parsley; cook for 3 minutes until the shrimp turns pink.
Add the flour noodles; gently toss until they absorb the liquid.
Stir in the blanched vegetables; cook for 1 to 2 minutes.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve immediately.

name: Filipino Style Spaghetti
description: Sweet-style spaghetti with ground pork, hotdogs, and cheese, a favorite for kids.
instructions: Cook the spaghetti noodles according to package directions; drain and set aside.
Heat oil in a pan; saute minced onion and garlic until the onion turns translucent.
Add ground pork and brown until a light brown color develops.
Stir in the minced luncheon meat and sliced hotdogs; cook for 2 to 3 minutes.
Pour in the spaghetti sauce and beef broth; stir well and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes to meld the flavors.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Pour the sauce over the cooked noodles and top with shredded cheddar cheese.
Serve hot.

name: Ginataang Gulay
description: Squash and string beans simmered in coconut milk with pork and shrimp.
rawIngredients: 6 ounces pork belly, sliced into small pieces
instructions: Boil water in a saucepan, add pork, cover, and cook on low to medium heat for 20 minutes.
Remove the pork from the saucepan and set aside; reserve the cooking water.
Heat oil in a pan and saute onion and garlic until the onion softens.
Add the boiled pork and saute for 1 minute.
Pour in the coconut milk and reserved water, then bring to a boil.
Add kalabasa, cover, and cook for 3 minutes.
Add shrimp and sitaw, cover, and continue cooking for 5 to 7 minutes.
Season with salt and transfer to a serving plate.

name: Chicken Afritada
description: Chicken braised in tomato sauce with potatoes, carrots, and bell pepper, a comforting everyday Filipino stew.
rawIngredients: 2 lbs chicken, cut into serving pieces
instructions: Marinate the chicken in soy sauce for 15 minutes.
Heat cooking oil in a pot and pan-fry the chicken pieces for 2 minutes per side, then set aside.
Using the same oil, saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Return the chicken to the pot and pour in the remaining marinade and tomato sauce.
Add water and bay leaves; bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Add potatoes and carrots; cook for 10 minutes.
Add bell peppers; season with salt and pepper and cook for 5 more minutes.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve hot with rice.

name: Sinigang na Manok
description: Chicken simmered in a sour tamarind broth with vegetables, a comforting everyday Filipino soup.
rawIngredients: 2 lbs chicken, cut into serving pieces
10 pieces string beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Combine chicken and water in a pot; bring to a boil, skimming off any scum.
Add onion and tomatoes; simmer for 10 minutes until the chicken is nearly tender.
Stir in the sinigang mix and season with fish sauce.
Add the daikon radish; cook for 8 minutes.
Add string beans and long green chili; cook for 5 minutes.
Add the kangkong last and simmer for 2 minutes until just wilted.
Season with salt to taste.
Transfer to a serving bowl and serve hot with rice.

name: Filipino Fried Chicken
description: Crispy fried chicken marinated in calamansi and soy sauce, a Filipino household favorite.
rawIngredients: 2 lbs chicken, cut into serving pieces
instructions: Combine chicken, soy sauce, calamansi juice, and garlic in a bowl; marinate for at least 1 hour.
Drain the chicken, reserving the marinade.
Season the flour with salt and pepper.
Dredge each piece of marinated chicken in the seasoned flour, shaking off the excess.
Heat cooking oil in a deep pan over medium heat.
Fry the chicken in batches for 10 to 12 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with rice and spiced vinegar.

name: Sinigang na Baboy
description: Pork ribs simmered in a sour tamarind broth with mixed vegetables.
instructions: Combine pork and water in a pot; bring to a boil, skimming off any scum.
Add onion and tomatoes; cover and simmer for 40 minutes until the pork is tender.
Stir in the sinigang mix and season with fish sauce.
Add the daikon radish and eggplant; cook for 8 minutes.
Add the okra; cook for 5 minutes.
Add the kangkong last and simmer for 2 minutes until just wilted.
Season with salt to taste.
Transfer to a serving bowl and serve hot with rice.

name: Filipino Pork BBQ Skewers
description: Sweet and savory grilled pork skewers marinated in soy sauce, banana ketchup, and calamansi.
instructions: Combine pork, soy sauce, banana ketchup, brown sugar, calamansi juice, garlic, and pepper in a bowl; mix well.
Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 3 hours, or overnight for best results.
Thread the marinated pork onto bamboo skewers.
Preheat a grill over medium heat.
Grill the skewers for 4 to 5 minutes per side, basting with the remaining marinade, until cooked through and lightly charred.
Serve hot with steamed rice and spiced vinegar.

name: Lechon Kawali
description: Deep-fried pork belly boiled until tender then fried until the skin turns golden and crackling.
instructions: Combine pork belly, bay leaves, peppercorns, water, and salt in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 45 minutes until the pork is fork-tender.
Remove the pork from the pot and let it air dry for at least 20 minutes.
Heat cooking oil in a deep pan over medium-high heat.
Carefully lower the pork into the hot oil and fry for 8 to 10 minutes per side until golden brown and crisp.
Drain on a wire rack and let rest for 5 minutes.
Chop into serving pieces and serve with lechon sauce or spiced vinegar.

name: Bistek Tagalog
description: Thin beef slices marinated in calamansi and soy sauce, pan-seared and topped with sweet onion rings.
instructions: Combine beef, soy sauce, and calamansi juice in a bowl; marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Drain the beef, reserving the marinade.
Heat 1 tablespoon of cooking oil in a pan; saute the onion rings for 1 minute until slightly softened, then set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the pan and saute garlic until light brown.
Add the marinated beef and cook for 2 minutes per side.
Pour in the reserved marinade and water; simmer for 5 minutes until the beef is tender.
Season with pepper and top with the sauteed onion rings.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve hot with rice.

name: Laing
description: Dried taro leaves slow-cooked in coconut milk with pork and shrimp paste.
rawIngredients: 1/2 lb pork belly, sliced into thin strips
instructions: Combine coconut milk, pork belly, shrimp paste, ginger, onion, and garlic in a pot; bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the dried taro leaves on top without stirring; let them soak up the coconut milk for 20 minutes.
Once the leaves have softened, gently stir to combine.
Add the coconut cream and thai chili pepper; continue cooking for 10 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Season with salt to taste.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve hot with rice.

name: Chopsuey
description: Stir-fried mixed vegetables with chicken and shrimp in a light savory sauce.
instructions: Heat cooking oil in a wok; saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add chicken and cook for 3 minutes until lightly browned.
Add shrimp and cook for 2 minutes until pink.
Pour in chicken broth and oyster sauce; bring to a simmer.
Add carrot and cauliflower; cook for 3 minutes.
Add bell peppers, snap peas, and cabbage; cook for 3 minutes until vegetables are crisp-tender.
Season with pepper.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve hot with rice.

name: Ginisang Munggo
description: Mung beans simmered until soft with pork, kalabasa, and malunggay leaves.
instructions: Boil the mung beans in water for 20 minutes until soft; set aside.
Heat cooking oil in a pot; saute garlic, onion, and tomatoes until softened.
Add pork and cook for 5 minutes until lightly browned.
Pour in the boiled mung beans with its cooking liquid; bring to a boil.
Add kalabasa and simmer for 8 minutes until tender.
Season with fish sauce and pepper.
Stir in the malunggay leaves and cook for 1 minute.
Transfer to a serving bowl and serve hot with rice.

name: Ginataang Hipon
description: Shrimp simmered in coconut milk with ginger, garlic, and chili peppers.
instructions: Heat a pan over medium heat; saute garlic, ginger, and onion until fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk; bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the coconut milk reduces slightly.
Add the shrimp and long green chili; cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the shrimp turns pink.
Season with fish sauce and pepper.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve hot with rice.

name: Sinigang na Hipon
description: Shrimp in a sour tamarind broth with radish, string beans, and kangkong.
rawIngredients: 10 pieces string beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Combine water, onion, and tomatoes in a pot; bring to a boil.
Add the daikon radish; cook for 8 minutes.
Stir in the sinigang mix.
Add the string beans; cook for 5 minutes.
Add the shrimp; cook for 3 minutes until pink.
Add the kangkong last and simmer for 2 minutes until just wilted.
Season with salt to taste.
Transfer to a serving bowl and serve hot with rice.

name: Inihaw na Bangus
description: Whole milkfish stuffed with tomatoes and onions, grilled until smoky and tender.
instructions: Combine tomatoes, onion, and ginger in a bowl; season with salt and pepper.
Stuff the mixture into the cavity of each cleaned milkfish.
Season the outside of the fish with salt.
Preheat a grill over medium heat.
Grill the fish for 8 to 10 minutes per side until the skin is lightly charred and the flesh is cooked through.
Combine calamansi juice and soy sauce in a small bowl for dipping.
Serve hot with the dipping sauce and warm rice.

name: Tortang Talong
description: Grilled eggplant dipped in beaten egg and pan-fried until golden.
instructions: Grill the eggplants directly over an open flame, turning occasionally, until the skin is charred and the flesh is soft.
Let the eggplants cool, then peel off the charred skin, keeping the stems intact.
Flatten each eggplant gently with a fork.
Beat the eggs in a bowl; season with salt and pepper.
Heat cooking oil in a pan over medium heat.
Dip each flattened eggplant into the beaten egg, coating well.
Fry for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Serve hot with rice and ketchup or soy sauce with calamansi.

name: Tortang Giniling
description: Ground pork sauteed with vegetables, folded into a hearty egg omelet.
instructions: Heat cooking oil in a pan; saute garlic, onion, and tomato until softened.
Add ground pork and cook for 5 minutes until browned.
Stir in carrot; cook for 3 minutes until slightly tender.
Season with salt and pepper; remove from heat and let cool slightly.
Beat the eggs in a bowl and mix in the cooked ground pork mixture.
Heat a lightly oiled pan over medium heat.
Pour in the egg mixture and cook for 3 to 4 minutes per side until set and golden.
Slice and serve hot with rice and banana ketchup.

name: Pancit Bihon
description: Rice noodles stir-fried with pork, vegetables, and soy sauce, a Filipino party staple.
rawIngredients: 10 pieces string beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Soak the rice noodles in water for 10 minutes until pliable; drain well.
Heat cooking oil in a wok; saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add pork and cook for 3 minutes until lightly browned.
Pour in chicken broth and soy sauce; bring to a boil.
Add carrot, cabbage, and string beans; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add shrimp; cook for 2 minutes until pink.
Add the soaked rice noodles; toss gently until they absorb the liquid.
Season with salt and cook for 2 more minutes.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve hot with calamansi.

name: Pancit Palabok
description: Rice noodles topped with a rich shrimp and annatto sauce, chicharon, and boiled egg.
instructions: Soak the rice noodles in water until softened; drain and briefly blanch in boiling water, then set aside.
Heat cooking oil in a pan; saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth and annatto seeds; simmer for 5 minutes, then strain out the seeds.
Add shrimp and cook for 2 minutes until pink; remove and set aside for topping.
Dissolve cornstarch in a little water and stir into the sauce; cook until thickened.
Season the sauce with fish sauce.
Arrange the noodles on a serving platter and pour the sauce over them.
Top with the cooked shrimp, crumbled chicharon, and sliced hard-boiled eggs.
Serve immediately with calamansi.

name: Lumpiang Shanghai
description: Crispy fried spring rolls filled with seasoned ground pork and vegetables.
instructions: Combine ground pork, carrot, onion, garlic, and egg in a bowl.
Season with salt and pepper; mix well until evenly combined.
Lay a spring roll wrapper on a flat surface and spoon a small amount of filling near one edge.
Roll tightly, folding in the sides, and seal the edge with a bit of water.
Repeat with the remaining wrappers and filling.
Heat cooking oil in a pan over medium heat.
Fry the rolls in batches for 3 to 4 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and slice diagonally.
Serve hot with sweet and sour sauce or banana ketchup.

name: Chicken Inasal
description: Grilled chicken marinated in vinegar, calamansi, and annatto oil, a Bacolod specialty.
rawIngredients: 2 lbs chicken, cut into serving pieces
instructions: Combine vinegar, calamansi juice, garlic, ginger, brown sugar, and salt in a bowl to make the marinade.
Add the chicken and turn to coat; cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours, or overnight for best results.
Combine the cooking oil and annatto powder in a small bowl to make the basting oil; set aside.
Preheat a grill over medium heat.
Remove the chicken from the marinade and grill for 8 to 10 minutes per side, basting frequently with the annatto oil.
Continue grilling and basting until the chicken is cooked through and lightly charred.
Serve hot with rice and a calamansi-soy dipping sauce.

name: Adobong Puti
description: A soy-sauce-free chicken adobo simmered in vinegar, garlic, and peppercorns for a brighter, tangier flavor.
rawIngredients: 2 lbs chicken, cut into serving pieces
instructions: Heat cooking oil in a pot; saute half the garlic until fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook for 3 minutes per side until lightly browned.
Add the remaining garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns.
Pour in the vinegar and water; bring to a boil without stirring.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 25 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Season with salt and simmer uncovered for 5 more minutes to reduce the sauce slightly.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve hot with rice.

name: Sweet and Sour Chicken
description: Crispy fried chicken tossed in a tangy pineapple and bell pepper sauce sweetened with banana ketchup.
rawIngredients: 2 lbs chicken, cut into serving pieces
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper, then dredge in flour.
Heat cooking oil in a pan and fry the chicken in batches for 8 to 10 minutes until golden and cooked through; drain and set aside.
In a separate pan, saute onion and bell peppers for 2 minutes.
Add the pineapple chunks, banana ketchup, and vinegar; bring to a simmer.
Dissolve the cornstarch in a little water and stir into the sauce along with the sugar; cook until thickened.
Add the fried chicken and toss to coat evenly in the sauce.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve hot with rice.

name: Humba
description: Visayan braised pork belly sweetened with brown sugar and fermented black beans.
instructions: Heat cooking oil in a pot; saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the pork belly and cook for 5 minutes until lightly browned on all sides.
Pour in the soy sauce, vinegar, and water; add the bay leaves and peppercorns.
Bring to a boil without stirring, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 1 hour until the pork is tender.
Stir in the brown sugar and fermented black beans.
Continue simmering uncovered for 20 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve hot with rice.

name: Crispy Pata
description: Whole pork leg boiled until tender then deep-fried until the skin turns golden and crackling.
instructions: Combine the pork leg, bay leaves, peppercorns, garlic, water, and salt in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 1 hour 30 minutes until the pork is fork-tender.
Remove the pork leg from the pot and let it air dry for at least 30 minutes.
Heat cooking oil in a large, deep pot over medium-high heat.
Carefully lower the pork leg into the hot oil and fry for 10 to 12 minutes per side until the skin is golden brown and crisp.
Drain on a wire rack and let rest for 5 minutes.
Chop into serving pieces and serve with a soy-vinegar dipping sauce.

name: Igado
description: An Ilocano stew of pork strips and liver braised in soy sauce and vinegar with bell peppers and carrots.
rawIngredients: 1/2 lb pig liver, sliced into strips
instructions: Heat cooking oil in a pan; saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the pork and cook for 5 minutes until lightly browned.
Pour in the soy sauce and vinegar; add the bay leaves and bring to a boil without stirring.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes until the pork is tender, adding water as needed.
Add the liver and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the carrot and bell peppers; season with pepper and cook for 5 more minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve hot with rice.

name: Bulalo
description: Beef shank and bone marrow slow-simmered into a clear, rich soup with corn and vegetables.
rawIngredients: 3 lbs beef shank, with bone marrow
instructions: Combine the beef shank and water in a large pot; bring to a boil, skimming off any scum.
Add the onion, cover, and simmer for 2 hours until the beef is tender and the marrow has softened.
Add the corn and potatoes; cook for 15 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and salt.
Add the cabbage and pechay; simmer for 3 minutes until just wilted.
Transfer to a serving bowl and serve hot with rice.

name: Beef Mechado
description: Beef chunks braised in tomato sauce and soy sauce with potatoes and carrots.
instructions: Combine the beef, soy sauce, and calamansi juice in a bowl; marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat cooking oil in a pot; saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Drain the beef, reserving the marinade, and add to the pot; cook for 5 minutes until lightly browned.
Pour in the tomato sauce, reserved marinade, water, and bay leaves.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 1 hour 15 minutes until the beef is tender.
Add the potatoes and carrots; season with pepper and cook for 15 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve hot with rice.

name: Beef Pares
description: Sweet braised beef brisket in a soy and star anise sauce, traditionally served with garlic rice and clear soup.
instructions: Combine the beef brisket and water in a pot; bring to a boil, skimming off any scum.
Add the onion, peppercorns, and fish sauce; cover and simmer for 45 minutes until the beef is tender, reserving the broth.
Drain the beef, keeping the broth aside for soup.
Heat cooking oil in a pan; saute garlic until golden.
Add the beef, soy sauce, brown sugar, and star anise; simmer for 20 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the meat.
Serve hot with garlic fried rice and a bowl of the reserved broth on the side.

name: Beef Tapa
description: Thin beef slices marinated in soy sauce and calamansi, pan-fried until caramelized.
instructions: Combine the beef, soy sauce, calamansi juice, garlic, brown sugar, and pepper in a bowl.
Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours, or overnight for best results.
Heat cooking oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Add the beef along with the marinade and cook for 3 to 4 minutes per side until browned and the liquid has mostly evaporated.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve hot with fried rice and a fried egg.

name: Paksiw na Bangus
description: Milkfish simmered in vinegar with ginger and long green chili for a tangy, savory finish.
instructions: Arrange the milkfish slices in a single layer in a wide pot.
Add the ginger, garlic, and long green chili on top.
Pour in the vinegar and water; add the eggplant.
Bring to a boil without stirring, then cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Season with salt and continue simmering for 5 more minutes until the sauce reduces slightly.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve hot with rice.

name: Escabeche
description: Whole fried fish smothered in a sweet and sour sauce with bell peppers and carrots.
instructions: Season the tilapia with salt.
Heat cooking oil in a pan and fry the fish for 5 to 6 minutes per side until golden and crisp; drain and set aside.
In a separate pan, saute garlic, ginger, and onion until fragrant.
Add the carrot and bell peppers; cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the vinegar and stir in the sugar and banana ketchup.
Dissolve the cornstarch in a little water and add to the sauce; cook until thickened.
Pour the sauce over the fried fish and serve immediately.

name: Kinilaw
description: Fresh tuna cured in vinegar and calamansi with ginger, onion, and chili — no cooking required.
instructions: Combine the tuna cubes with vinegar in a bowl; let sit for 2 minutes, then drain off the vinegar.
Add the calamansi juice, onion, ginger, and chili.
Season with salt and toss gently to combine.
Cover and refrigerate for 10 minutes before serving.
Serve chilled as a starter or side dish.

name: Adobong Pusit
description: Squid braised adobo-style in its own ink for a rich, savory sauce.
instructions: Heat cooking oil in a pan; saute garlic, onion, and tomatoes until softened.
Add the squid and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the vinegar and let it boil without stirring for 2 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, bay leaves, and water; season with pepper.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes until the squid is tender and the sauce has darkened.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve hot with rice.

name: Lumpiang Togue
description: Crispy fried spring rolls filled with bean sprouts, carrots, and ground pork.
rawIngredients: 10 pieces string beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Heat a small amount of cooking oil in a pan; saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the ground pork and cook for 5 minutes until lightly browned.
Add the carrot and string beans; cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the bean sprouts and season with fish sauce and pepper; cook for 1 minute, then remove from heat and let cool.
Lay a spring roll wrapper on a flat surface and spoon a small amount of filling near one edge.
Roll tightly, folding in the sides, and seal the edge with a bit of water.
Repeat with the remaining wrappers and filling.
Heat the remaining cooking oil in a pan and fry the rolls in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until golden brown and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and serve with a spiced vinegar dip.

name: Ginisang Ampalaya
description: Sauteed bitter gourd with tomatoes, egg, and dried shrimp for a classic everyday vegetable dish.
instructions: Sprinkle the sliced ampalaya with salt, let sit for 10 minutes, then rinse and squeeze out the excess liquid.
Heat cooking oil in a pan; saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and dried shrimp; cook for 2 minutes until the tomatoes soften.
Add the ampalaya and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Beat the eggs and pour over the vegetables; stir gently until the eggs are just set.
Season with salt to taste.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve hot with rice.

name: Sopas
description: Creamy chicken and macaroni soup with vegetables and evaporated milk.
instructions: Heat cooking oil in a pot; saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the shredded chicken and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the chicken broth; bring to a boil.
Add the carrot and celery; simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the elbow macaroni and cook for 10 minutes until tender, stirring occasionally.
Reduce heat to low and stir in the evaporated milk.
Season with salt and pepper; simmer for 2 minutes without boiling.
Transfer to a serving bowl and serve hot.

name: Pancit Molo
description: A comforting soup of pork and shrimp dumplings in a rich chicken broth, an Ilonggo classic.
instructions: Combine the ground pork, shrimp, half the onion, and half the garlic in a bowl; season with pepper.
Place a teaspoon of the filling onto each wrapper and fold into small dumplings, sealing the edges with a bit of water.
Heat cooking oil in a pot; saute the remaining garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the shredded chicken and fish sauce; cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Drop in the dumplings and simmer gently for 10 minutes until they float and are cooked through.
Transfer to a serving bowl and serve hot, garnished with fried garlic if desired.

name: Tortang Itlog
description: A simple everyday omelette of eggs, tomato, and onion, ready in minutes.
instructions: Beat the eggs in a bowl.
Stir in the tomato and onion; season with salt and pepper.
Heat cooking oil in a pan over medium heat.
Pour in the egg mixture and cook for 2 to 3 minutes per side until set and lightly golden.
Slice and serve hot with rice.

name: Dinuguan
description: A savory pork stew simmered in vinegar and pig's blood, often called 'chocolate meat.'
instructions: Heat cooking oil in a pot; saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the pork belly and cook for 5 minutes until lightly browned.
Pour in the water, cover, and simmer for 25 minutes until the pork is tender.
Add the vinegar and long green chili; bring to a boil without stirring.
Stir in the pig blood gradually, simmering on low heat until the sauce thickens.
Season with salt to taste.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve hot with rice or puto.

name: Longganisa
description: Homemade sweet-garlicky Filipino breakfast sausage, pan-fried until caramelized.
instructions: Combine the ground pork, brown sugar, garlic, vinegar, salt, and pepper in a bowl; mix well.
Cover and let the mixture cure in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, or overnight for best flavor.
Shape the mixture into small logs, about 2 inches long.
Heat cooking oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add the sausages and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through.
Serve hot with fried rice and a fried egg.

name: Embutido
description: A Filipino-style steamed meatloaf of ground pork, carrots, and raisins, studded with egg and sausage.
instructions: Combine the ground pork, carrot, raisins, banana ketchup, onion, salt, and pepper in a bowl; mix well.
Lay out a sheet of foil and spread a portion of the pork mixture into a rectangle.
Arrange sliced hard-boiled eggs and hotdogs down the center.
Roll the mixture into a log using the foil, twisting the ends to seal tightly.
Repeat with the remaining mixture to form additional logs.
Steam the logs for 45 minutes until firm and cooked through.
Let cool slightly, then slice and serve, or pan-fry the slices for a crisp exterior.

name: Ukoy
description: Crispy shrimp and vegetable fritters, best served hot with a spiced vinegar dip.
instructions: Combine the flour, cornstarch, salt, and water in a bowl until smooth.
Stir in the bean sprouts and carrot.
Heat cooking oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Scoop a portion of the batter into the pan and top with a few pieces of shrimp, pressing gently to adhere.
Fry for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden brown and crisp.
Repeat with the remaining batter and shrimp.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with a spiced vinegar dip.

name: Chicken Curry
description: Chicken simmered in coconut milk and curry powder with potatoes, carrots, and bell pepper.
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook until lightly browned on all sides.
Stir in the curry powder and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the water and fish sauce, then bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the potatoes and carrot, and simmer for 10 minutes more.
Pour in the coconut milk and add the bell pepper.
Simmer uncovered for 5 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly, then serve.

name: Garlic Butter Chicken
description: Pan-seared chicken thighs finished in a rich garlic butter sauce.
instructions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a pan and sear the chicken until golden and cooked through, then set aside.
In the same pan, melt the butter and saute the garlic until golden and fragrant.
Return the chicken to the pan and add the soy sauce.
Toss the chicken in the garlic butter sauce for 2 minutes.
Serve hot, spooning the garlic butter over the chicken.

name: Chicken Pastel
description: Creamy chicken stew with vegetables and hotdog slices in a savory milk-based sauce.
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and saute garlic and onion.
Add the chicken and soy sauce, then cook until lightly browned.
Pour in the chicken broth and simmer for 15 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Add the potatoes and carrot, and cook for 10 minutes.
Stir in the hotdog slices and green peas.
Pour in the evaporated milk and season with salt.
Simmer for 5 minutes until the sauce thickens, then serve.

name: Chicken Pochero
description: Hearty chicken and vegetable stew in a tomato broth, sweetened with saba banana.
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and saute garlic, onion, and tomatoes until softened.
Add the chicken and cook until lightly browned.
Pour in the water and fish sauce, then bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Add the potatoes and saba banana, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the cabbage and simmer for 3 minutes more.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Chicken Sotanghon Soup
description: Comforting glass noodle soup with shredded chicken, ginger, and malunggay leaves.
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and saute garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the water and fish sauce, then bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the chicken is tender, then shred the meat.
Soak the sotanghon noodles in water until softened, then drain.
Add the noodles to the pot and simmer for 3 minutes.
Stir in the malunggay leaves and turn off the heat before serving.

name: Chicken Binakol
description: Chicken soup simmered in coconut water with lemongrass and young coconut meat.
instructions: Combine the chicken, coconut water, lemongrass, ginger, and onion in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer for 20 minutes.
Season with fish sauce.
Add the chili pepper and simmer for 5 minutes more.
Stir in the malunggay leaves and turn off the heat.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Chicken Halang-Halang
description: Spicy Visayan chicken stew in coconut milk with turmeric and chili.
instructions: Combine the chicken, garlic, onion, ginger, lemongrass, and turmeric powder in a pot with enough water to cover.
Bring to a boil, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the kalabasa and simmer for 10 minutes until tender.
Pour in the coconut milk and season with fish sauce.
Add the chili peppers and simmer for 5 minutes.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Honey Garlic Chicken
description: Crispy pan-fried chicken pieces coated in a sticky honey garlic glaze.
instructions: Season the chicken lightly and dust with cornstarch.
Heat oil in a pan and fry the chicken until golden and cooked through, then set aside.
In the same pan, saute the garlic until fragrant.
Add the honey, soy sauce, and water, then simmer until slightly thickened.
Return the chicken to the pan and toss to coat in the sauce.
Cook for 2 minutes more, then serve.

name: Orange Chicken (Filipino style)
description: Crispy fried chicken bites tossed in a tangy-sweet orange sauce.
instructions: Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces and dust with cornstarch.
Heat oil in a pan and fry the chicken until golden and crisp, then set aside.
In a saucepan, combine the orange juice, brown sugar, soy sauce, garlic, and water.
Simmer the sauce until slightly thickened.
Toss the fried chicken in the sauce until well coated.
Serve immediately while the chicken is still crisp.

name: Lemon Chicken
description: Crispy fried chicken fillets glazed in a bright lemon sauce.
instructions: Season the chicken and dust with cornstarch.
Heat oil in a pan and fry the chicken until golden and cooked through, then set aside.
In a saucepan, combine the lemon juice, sugar, soy sauce, and water.
Simmer the sauce until slightly thickened.
Pour the sauce over the fried chicken just before serving.

name: Soy Garlic Chicken
description: Crispy fried chicken tossed in a savory soy garlic glaze with sesame seeds.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and fry the chicken until golden and cooked through, then set aside.
In the same pan, saute the garlic until fragrant.
Add the soy sauce and brown sugar, then simmer until slightly thickened.
Return the chicken to the pan and toss to coat.
Drizzle with sesame oil and sprinkle with sesame seeds before serving.

name: Chicken Teriyaki
description: Pan-grilled chicken thighs glazed in a sweet and savory teriyaki sauce.
instructions: Combine the soy sauce, brown sugar, garlic, sesame oil, and water in a bowl to make the marinade.
Marinate the chicken for at least 20 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan and cook the chicken, reserving the marinade.
Once the chicken is browned on both sides, pour in the reserved marinade.
Simmer until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce thickens.
Slice and serve over rice.

name: Chicken Tocino
description: Sweet cured chicken slices, pan-fried until caramelized at the edges.
instructions: Combine the chicken, sugar, soy sauce, pineapple juice, annatto seeds, and salt in a bowl.
Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, or overnight for best results.
Heat oil in a pan and add the marinated chicken along with the water.
Simmer until the water evaporates and the chicken is cooked through.
Continue cooking until the chicken caramelizes and browns slightly at the edges.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Chicken Hamonado
description: Chicken braised in a sweet pineapple and soy sauce until tender.
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook until lightly browned.
Pour in the pineapple juice, soy sauce, brown sugar, and water.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 25 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce thickens slightly.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Chicken with Oyster Sauce
description: Stir-fried chicken and vegetables coated in a savory oyster sauce glaze.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook until lightly browned.
Add the carrot and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the oyster sauce, soy sauce, and water.
Simmer until the chicken is cooked through.
Add the bell pepper and cornstarch slurry, then cook until the sauce thickens.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Pork Adobo
description: Classic pork braised in soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, and bay leaves until tender.
instructions: Combine the pork, soy sauce, and garlic in a pot and marinate for 15 minutes.
Add the water, bay leaves, and peppercorns, then bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer for 30 minutes until the pork is tender.
Add the vinegar and let it boil without stirring for 2 minutes.
Stir in the sugar and simmer uncovered until the sauce reduces slightly.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Pork Giniling
description: Ground pork sauteed with potatoes, carrots, and tomato sauce.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the ground pork and cook until browned, breaking it apart as it cooks.
Stir in the soy sauce and tomato sauce.
Add the potatoes, carrot, and water.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Pork Steak
description: Pan-fried pork chops smothered in a soy sauce and onion gravy, Filipino bistek-style.
instructions: Combine the pork, soy sauce, lemon juice, and pepper in a bowl and marinate for 20 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan and fry the pork until browned on both sides, reserving the marinade.
Remove the pork and set aside.
In the same pan, saute the onion until softened.
Return the pork to the pan along with the reserved marinade and water.
Simmer until the pork is tender and the sauce reduces, then serve.

name: Pork Estofado
description: Pork braised in a sweet soy sauce with saba bananas and fried potatoes.
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the pork belly and cook until lightly browned.
Pour in the soy sauce, brown sugar, water, and bay leaves.
Cover and simmer for 30 minutes until the pork is tender.
Fry the potatoes and saba banana separately until golden, then add to the pot.
Simmer for 5 minutes more, then serve.

name: Pork Hamonado
description: Pork belly braised in pineapple juice and soy sauce until sweet and tender.
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the pork and cook until lightly browned.
Pour in the pineapple juice, soy sauce, brown sugar, water, and bay leaves.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 30 minutes until the pork is tender.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce thickens slightly, then serve.

name: Pork Asado
description: Pork strips braised in a sweet soy sauce marinade until fork-tender.
instructions: Combine the pork, soy sauce, lemon juice, and garlic in a bowl and marinate for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a pot and saute the onion until softened.
Add the pork along with the marinade and cook until lightly browned.
Pour in the water, brown sugar, and bay leaves.
Cover and simmer for 30 minutes until the pork is tender and the sauce thickens.
Slice and serve with steamed rice.

name: Fried Liempo
description: Pork belly slices marinated in soy sauce and calamansi, then deep-fried until crisp.
instructions: Combine the pork belly, soy sauce, calamansi juice, garlic, pepper, and salt in a bowl.
Marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat cooking oil in a pan over medium heat.
Fry the pork belly until deeply golden and crisp, about 8 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels, then slice and serve with a vinegar dip.

name: Binagoongan Baboy
description: Pork braised in shrimp paste and vinegar with tomatoes and a touch of sugar.
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and saute garlic, onion, and tomatoes until softened.
Add the pork and cook until lightly browned.
Pour in the water and vinegar, then bring to a boil without stirring for 2 minutes.
Cover and simmer for 25 minutes until the pork is tender.
Stir in the shrimp paste and sugar.
Simmer uncovered for 5 minutes, then serve.

name: Sweet and Sour Pork
description: Crispy fried pork tossed with bell pepper and pineapple in a tangy sweet sauce.
instructions: Cut the pork into cubes and coat lightly with cornstarch.
Heat oil in a pan and fry the pork until golden and cooked through, then set aside.
In a saucepan, combine the tomato sauce, sugar, vinegar, and water.
Simmer the sauce until it starts to thicken.
Add the bell pepper and pineapple chunks, and cook for 2 minutes.
Toss in the fried pork and coat well with the sauce before serving.

name: Pork with Oyster Sauce
description: Stir-fried pork strips and vegetables coated in a savory oyster sauce glaze.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the pork and cook until lightly browned.
Add the carrot and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the oyster sauce, soy sauce, and water.
Simmer until the pork is cooked through.
Add the bell pepper and cornstarch slurry, then cook until the sauce thickens.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Garlic Pork
description: Deep-fried pork cubes tossed with crispy toasted garlic bits.
instructions: Season the pork with soy sauce, salt, and pepper, and marinate for 15 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan and fry the pork until golden and crisp, then drain and set aside.
In a separate pan with a little oil, fry the minced garlic until golden and crispy.
Toss the fried pork with the toasted garlic bits.
Serve hot with a vinegar dipping sauce.

name: Salt and Pepper Pork
description: Crispy fried pork bites seasoned simply with salt, pepper, and garlic.
instructions: Cut the pork into bite-sized pieces and season with half the salt and pepper.
Dust the pork with cornstarch.
Heat oil in a pan and fry the pork until golden and crisp, then drain.
In a separate pan with a little oil, saute the garlic and bell pepper.
Toss the fried pork with the sauteed garlic and bell pepper, and the remaining salt and pepper.
Serve hot.

name: Pork Caldereta
description: Pork braised in tomato sauce and liver spread with potatoes, carrots, and bell pepper.
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the pork and cook until lightly browned.
Pour in the tomato sauce, water, and bay leaves.
Cover and simmer for 30 minutes until the pork is tender.
Add the potatoes and carrot, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the liver spread and bell pepper.
Simmer for 5 minutes more, then serve.

name: Pork Pochero
description: Pork and vegetable stew in a tomato broth, sweetened with saba banana.
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and saute garlic, onion, and tomatoes until softened.
Add the pork and cook until lightly browned.
Pour in the water and fish sauce, then bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer for 25 minutes until the pork is tender.
Add the potatoes and saba banana, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the cabbage and simmer for 3 minutes more.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Pork Binagoongan with Talong
description: Pork and eggplant braised in shrimp paste with tomatoes and a touch of vinegar.
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and saute garlic, onion, and tomatoes until softened.
Add the pork and cook until lightly browned.
Pour in the water and vinegar, then boil without stirring for 2 minutes.
Cover and simmer for 25 minutes until the pork is tender.
Add the eggplant and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the shrimp paste and sugar, then simmer for 3 minutes more before serving.

name: Fried Tilapia
description: Whole tilapia seasoned with salt and fried until the skin is golden and crisp.
instructions: Clean the tilapia and pat dry with paper towels.
Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat the cooking oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Fry the tilapia for 5 to 6 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and serve with a vinegar dip.

name: Ginataang Tilapia
description: Tilapia simmered in coconut milk with ginger, chili, and spinach.
instructions: Arrange the ginger, onion, and garlic at the bottom of a pot.
Place the tilapia on top and pour in the coconut milk.
Bring to a gentle boil, then simmer for 12 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and add the chili peppers.
Add the spinach and simmer for 2 minutes more.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Daing na Bangus
description: Butterflied milkfish marinated in vinegar and garlic, then fried until crisp.
instructions: Combine the vinegar, garlic, pepper, and salt in a bowl.
Marinate the milkfish in the mixture for at least 30 minutes.
Heat cooking oil in a pan over medium heat.
Fry the milkfish until golden and crisp on both sides.
Drain on paper towels and serve with steamed rice.

name: Relyenong Bangus
description: Deboned milkfish stuffed with a savory sauteed filling of its own flaked meat and vegetables.
instructions: Carefully debone the milkfish, keeping the skin intact, and set aside the flesh.
Steam or boil the fish flesh until cooked, then flake it and remove any bones.
Saute garlic and onion, then add the flaked fish, carrot, and green peas.
Season with salt and pepper, then mix in the egg and bread crumbs.
Stuff the mixture back into the fish skin, reshaping it to look whole.
Heat oil in a pan and fry the stuffed fish until golden on all sides.
Slice and serve.

name: Garlic Butter Shrimp
description: Shrimp sauteed in garlic butter until pink and juicy.
instructions: Season the shrimp with salt and pepper.
Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat.
Saute the garlic until fragrant and lightly golden.
Add the shrimp and cook for 2 to 3 minutes per side until pink.
Squeeze in lemon juice and toss to coat before serving.

name: Buttered Shrimp
description: Crispy fried shrimp coated in a creamy buttered sauce with a hint of spice.
instructions: Season the shrimp with salt and coat lightly in cornstarch.
Heat cooking oil in a pan and fry the shrimp until crisp, then drain.
In a separate pan, melt the butter and saute the garlic and chili until fragrant.
Toss the fried shrimp in the garlic butter until well coated.
Serve hot immediately.

name: Adobong Tahong
description: Mussels simmered in garlic, soy sauce, and vinegar until they open and soak up the sauce.
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the mussels and soy sauce, and stir to coat.
Pour in the vinegar and let it boil without stirring for 2 minutes.
Cover and simmer for 8 minutes until the mussels open.
Season with pepper and discard any unopened mussels before serving.

name: Tahong Soup
description: Light ginger broth with mussels and spinach, comforting and quick to make.
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and saute garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant.
Pour in the water and fish sauce, then bring to a boil.
Add the mussels and simmer for 8 minutes until they open.
Add the spinach and simmer for 2 minutes more.
Discard any unopened mussels, then serve hot.

name: Steamed Tahong
description: Mussels steamed with ginger, lemongrass, and onion until they open.
instructions: Combine the ginger, lemongrass, onion, and water in a pot.
Bring to a boil.
Add the mussels, cover, and steam for 8 minutes until they open.
Discard any unopened mussels.
Serve hot with the steaming broth and a vinegar dip.

name: Baked Tahong
description: Half-shell mussels topped with a garlicky butter and cheese crust, baked until bubbly.
instructions: Steam the mussels until they open, then remove the top shells, keeping the meat on the bottom half.
Melt the butter and saute the garlic until fragrant.
Mix the garlic butter with the bread crumbs and pepper.
Top each mussel half with the mixture and sprinkle with cheese.
Bake or broil for 8 to 10 minutes until golden and bubbly.
Serve hot.

name: Sweet and Sour Fish
description: Crispy fried fish fillets topped with a tangy-sweet vegetable sauce.
instructions: Cut the fish into fillets and fry in hot oil until golden and crisp, then set aside.
In a saucepan, combine the tomato sauce, sugar, vinegar, and water.
Add the carrot and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the bell pepper and pineapple chunks, and simmer for 2 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook until the sauce thickens.
Pour the sauce over the fried fish before serving.

name: Fried Galunggong
description: Whole mackerel scad, seasoned and fried until crisp on the outside.
instructions: Clean the galunggong and pat dry.
Season with salt and pepper.
Heat cooking oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Fry the fish for 4 to 5 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and serve with a vinegar dip.

name: Pritong Hasa-Hasa
description: Short-bodied mackerel, seasoned and fried until golden and crisp.
instructions: Clean the hasa-hasa and pat dry.
Season with salt and pepper.
Heat cooking oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Fry the fish for 4 to 5 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and serve with a vinegar and chili dip.

name: Ginataang Galunggong
description: Mackerel scad simmered in coconut milk with ginger and chili.
instructions: Arrange the ginger, onion, and garlic at the bottom of a pot.
Place the galunggong on top and pour in the coconut milk.
Bring to a gentle boil, then simmer for 12 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and add the chili peppers.
Simmer for 3 minutes more, then serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Sardines with Misua
description: Comforting misua noodle soup simmered with canned sardines and tomatoes.
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and saute garlic, onion, and tomatoes until softened.
Add the sardines along with their sauce.
Pour in the water and fish sauce, then bring to a boil.
Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the misua noodles and simmer for 2 minutes until softened.
Serve hot.

name: Beef Giniling
description: Ground beef sauteed with potatoes, carrots, and tomato sauce.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the ground beef and cook until browned, breaking it apart as it cooks.
Stir in the soy sauce and tomato sauce.
Add the potatoes, carrot, and water.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Corned Beef Guisado
description: Canned corned beef sauteed with potatoes, onions, and garlic.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the diced potatoes and cook until lightly browned.
Stir in the corned beef and cook until heated through.
Season with pepper and cook for 3 minutes more.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Beef with Broccoli
description: Tender beef strips and broccoli stir-fried in a savory oyster sauce.
instructions: Slice the beef thinly against the grain and marinate with soy sauce for 10 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan and saute the garlic until fragrant.
Add the beef and stir-fry until browned.
Add the broccoli and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the oyster sauce and water.
Add the cornstarch slurry and cook until the sauce thickens, then serve.

name: Beef with Oyster Sauce
description: Stir-fried beef strips and vegetables coated in a savory oyster sauce glaze.
instructions: Slice the beef thinly against the grain and marinate with soy sauce for 10 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the beef and stir-fry until browned.
Add the carrot and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the oyster sauce and water.
Add the bell pepper and cornstarch slurry, then cook until the sauce thickens before serving.

name: Beef Picadillo
description: Ground beef simmered in a light tomato broth with potatoes and carrots.
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and saute garlic, onion, and tomatoes until softened.
Add the ground beef and cook until browned.
Pour in the water and fish sauce, then bring to a boil.
Add the potatoes and carrot.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Beef Stroganoff (Filipino style)
description: Beef strips and mushrooms in a creamy evaporated milk sauce over rice.
instructions: Slice the beef thinly against the grain.
Melt the butter in a pan and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the beef and cook until browned.
Add the mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the soy sauce and water, then simmer for 10 minutes until the beef is tender.
Pour in the evaporated milk and cornstarch slurry, and simmer until the sauce thickens.
Serve hot over rice.

name: Beef and Mushroom Stir Fry
description: Quick stir-fried beef and mushrooms in a garlicky soy sauce glaze.
instructions: Slice the beef thinly against the grain and marinate with soy sauce for 10 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the beef and stir-fry over high heat until browned.
Add the mushrooms and oyster sauce, and cook for 3 minutes.
Season with pepper and serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Ginisang Kangkong
description: Water spinach quickly sauteed with garlic, tomatoes, and shrimp paste.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and saute garlic, onion, and tomatoes until softened.
Add the shrimp paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the kangkong and toss until just wilted.
Cook for 2 minutes more, then serve hot.

name: Ginisang Pechay
description: Bok choy sauteed with garlic, onion, and ground pork.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the ground pork and cook until browned.
Pour in the water and fish sauce, then simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the pechay and cook until just wilted.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Ginisang Repolyo
description: Cabbage sauteed with ground pork, carrots, and garlic.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the ground pork and cook until browned.
Add the carrot and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the water and fish sauce, then simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the cabbage and cook until just wilted, then serve.

name: Ginisang Sayote
description: Chayote sauteed with ground pork and garlic in a light savory sauce.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the ground pork and cook until browned.
Add the sliced sayote and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the water and fish sauce.
Cover and simmer for 6 minutes until the sayote is tender, then serve.

name: Ginisang Kalabasa
description: Squash sauteed with ground pork, string beans, and garlic.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the ground pork and cook until browned.
Add the kalabasa and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the water and fish sauce.
Cover and simmer for 8 minutes until the kalabasa is tender.
Add the string beans and cook for 3 minutes more, then serve.

name: Ginisang Upo
description: Bottle gourd sauteed with shrimp, garlic, and tomatoes.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and saute garlic, onion, and tomatoes until softened.
Add the shrimp and cook until pink.
Add the sliced upo and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the water and fish sauce.
Cover and simmer for 6 minutes until the upo is tender, then serve.

name: Ginisang Patola
description: Sponge gourd sauteed with egg, garlic, and tomatoes.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and saute garlic, onion, and tomatoes until softened.
Add the sliced patola and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the water and fish sauce, then simmer for 5 minutes.
Crack in the eggs and stir gently until just set.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Ginisang Talbos ng Kamote
description: Sweet potato tops sauteed with garlic, onion, and shrimp paste.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and saute garlic, onion, and tomatoes until softened.
Add the shrimp paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the kamote tops and toss until just wilted.
Cook for 2 minutes more, then serve hot.

name: Adobong Sitaw
description: String beans braised adobo-style with pork, soy sauce, and vinegar.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the pork and cook until lightly browned.
Pour in the soy sauce, water, and bay leaf, then simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the vinegar and boil without stirring for 2 minutes.
Add the sitaw and cook for 4 minutes until just tender, then serve.

name: Ginataang Langka
description: Unripe jackfruit simmered in coconut milk with pork and shrimp paste.
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the pork and cook until lightly browned.
Add the langka and coconut milk, then bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook for 15 minutes until the langka and pork are tender.
Stir in the shrimp paste and chili peppers.
Simmer for 5 minutes more, then serve.

name: Ginataang Sitaw
description: String beans and squash simmered in coconut milk with shrimp.
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the kalabasa and coconut milk, then simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the sitaw and shrimp, and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the shrimp paste and simmer for 3 minutes more.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Ginataang Kalabasa
description: Squash and string beans simmered in coconut milk with dried shrimp.
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the dried shrimp and cook for 1 minute.
Add the kalabasa and coconut milk, then simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the string beans and season with fish sauce.
Simmer for 5 minutes more until the vegetables are tender, then serve.

name: Ensaladang Talong
description: Grilled eggplant salad tossed with tomatoes, onions, and a calamansi vinaigrette.
instructions: Grill the eggplants over open flame or a hot pan until the skin is charred and the flesh is soft.
Peel off the charred skin and slice the eggplant lengthwise.
Arrange the eggplant on a plate with sliced tomatoes and onion.
Whisk together the vinegar, calamansi juice, salt, and pepper.
Drizzle the dressing over the salad before serving.

name: Ensaladang Mangga
description: Shredded green mango salad tossed with tomatoes, onions, and shrimp paste.
instructions: Peel and shred the green mango.
Slice the tomatoes and onion thinly.
Combine the mango, tomatoes, and onion in a bowl.
Serve with shrimp paste on the side for dipping or mixed in.

name: Tortang Okra
description: Sliced okra bound in beaten egg and pan-fried until golden.
instructions: Slice the okra thinly and combine with chopped onion in a bowl.
Beat the eggs and season with salt and pepper, then mix into the okra.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Scoop portions of the mixture into the pan and flatten slightly.
Fry for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden, then serve.

name: Tortang Sayote
description: Grated chayote bound in beaten egg and pan-fried into savory patties.
instructions: Grate the sayote and squeeze out excess liquid.
Combine with chopped onion in a bowl.
Beat the eggs and season with salt and pepper, then mix into the sayote.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Scoop portions of the mixture into the pan and flatten slightly.
Fry for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden, then serve.

name: Tortang Kalabasa
description: Grated squash bound in beaten egg and pan-fried into golden patties.
instructions: Grate the kalabasa and squeeze out excess liquid.
Combine with chopped onion in a bowl.
Beat the eggs and season with salt and pepper, then mix into the kalabasa.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Scoop portions of the mixture into the pan and flatten slightly.
Fry for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden, then serve.

name: Adobong Kangkong
description: Water spinach quickly braised in garlic, soy sauce, and vinegar.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the soy sauce and vinegar, and let it boil without stirring for 1 minute.
Add the kangkong and toss until just wilted.
Cook for 2 minutes more, then serve hot.

name: Stir-fried Mixed Vegetables
description: Colorful medley of vegetables stir-fried in garlic and oyster sauce.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and saute the garlic until fragrant.
Add the carrot and cauliflower, and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add the string beans and bell pepper.
Pour in the oyster sauce and water.
Cook for 3 minutes more until the vegetables are crisp-tender, then serve.

name: Garlic Butter Mushrooms
description: Mushrooms sauteed in garlic butter until golden and tender.
instructions: Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat.
Saute the garlic until fragrant and lightly golden.
Add the mushrooms and cook for 5 minutes until golden and tender.
Season with salt, pepper, and soy sauce.
Cook for 2 minutes more, then serve hot.

name: Scrambled Egg with Tomatoes
description: Fluffy scrambled eggs cooked with sauteed tomatoes and onion.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and saute the onion and tomatoes until softened.
Beat the eggs and season with salt and pepper.
Pour the eggs into the pan.
Stir gently and cook until just set.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Scrambled Egg with Sardines
description: Scrambled eggs cooked with flaked canned sardines and onion.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and saute the onion until softened.
Add the sardines and flake them with a spatula.
Beat the eggs and season with pepper, then pour into the pan.
Stir gently and cook until just set.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Itlog na Maalat at Kamatis
description: Sliced salted eggs and fresh tomatoes, a simple classic breakfast pairing.
instructions: Slice the salted eggs into wedges.
Slice the tomatoes and onion.
Arrange the eggs, tomatoes, and onion on a plate.
Serve with steamed rice.

name: Egg Fried Rice
description: Day-old rice stir-fried with egg, garlic, and green onion.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and saute the garlic until golden.
Push the garlic to one side, then scramble the eggs in the pan.
Add the rice and toss to combine with the garlic and egg.
Season with soy sauce and salt.
Stir in the chopped green onion and cook for 2 minutes more, then serve.

name: Egg Drop Soup
description: Light chicken broth thickened slightly and swirled with ribbons of egg.
instructions: Bring the chicken broth to a boil in a pot.
Dissolve the cornstarch in a little water and stir it into the broth to thicken slightly.
Beat the eggs in a bowl.
Slowly drizzle the eggs into the simmering broth while stirring gently to form ribbons.
Season with salt and pepper, and top with chopped green onion before serving.

name: Omelette with Cheese
description: Simple folded omelette filled with melted cheddar cheese.
instructions: Beat the eggs and season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Pour in the eggs and let the bottom set slightly.
Sprinkle the cheese over half of the omelette.
Fold the omelette in half and cook until the cheese melts, then serve.

name: Omelette with Spinach
description: Folded omelette filled with sauteed spinach and onion.
instructions: Heat a little oil in a pan and saute the onion and spinach until wilted, then set aside.
Beat the eggs and season with salt and pepper.
Heat the remaining oil in the pan and pour in the eggs.
Spoon the sauteed spinach over half of the omelette.
Fold the omelette in half and cook until set, then serve.

name: Omelette with Mushroom
description: Folded omelette filled with sauteed mushrooms and onion.
instructions: Heat a little oil in a pan and saute the onion and mushrooms until softened, then set aside.
Beat the eggs and season with salt and pepper.
Heat the remaining oil in the pan and pour in the eggs.
Spoon the sauteed mushrooms over half of the omelette.
Fold the omelette in half and cook until set, then serve.

name: Omelette with Ham
description: Folded omelette filled with diced ham and a sprinkle of cheese.
instructions: Dice the ham.
Beat the eggs and season with pepper.
Heat oil in a pan and pour in the eggs.
Scatter the ham and cheese over half of the omelette.
Fold the omelette in half and cook until the cheese melts, then serve.

name: Pancit Malabon
description: Thick rice noodles in a savory shrimp-based sauce, topped with shrimp and boiled egg.
instructions: Boil the eggs until hard-cooked, then peel and slice.
Soak the rice noodles in warm water until softened, then drain.
Heat oil in a pan and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the shrimp and squid, and cook until just done, then set most aside for topping.
Add the shrimp paste and water, and bring to a simmer.
Add the noodles and toss until the sauce is absorbed.
Top with the reserved shrimp, squid, and sliced egg before serving.

name: Pancit Lomi
description: Thick fresh egg noodles in a hearty, gently thickened pork and vegetable broth.
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the pork and cook until lightly browned.
Pour in the water and fish sauce, then simmer for 15 minutes until the pork is tender.
Add the carrot and cabbage, and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the lomi noodles and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and simmer until the broth thickens slightly, then serve.

name: Pancit Sotanghon
description: Glass noodles stir-fried with chicken, cabbage, and carrots.
instructions: Soak the sotanghon noodles in water until softened, then drain.
Heat oil in a pan and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook until lightly browned.
Pour in the chicken broth, soy sauce, and fish sauce, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the carrot and cabbage, and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the noodles and toss until the liquid is absorbed, then serve.

name: Miki Guisado
description: Fresh thick egg noodles stir-fried with pork, shrimp, and vegetables.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the pork and cook until lightly browned.
Add the shrimp and cook until pink.
Pour in the chicken broth and soy sauce, then add the carrot.
Simmer for 5 minutes, then add the cabbage and miki noodles.
Toss until the noodles absorb the sauce, then serve.

name: Batchoy
description: Miki noodles in a rich pork broth, topped with crushed chicharon and boiled egg.
instructions: Boil the eggs until hard-cooked, then peel and slice.
Heat oil in a pot and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the pork and cook until lightly browned.
Pour in the water and fish sauce, then simmer for 20 minutes until the pork is tender.
Slice the pork thinly and return to the pot.
Add the miki noodles and cook for 3 minutes.
Ladle into bowls and top with crushed chicharon and sliced egg before serving.

name: Chicken Mami
description: Egg noodle soup with shredded chicken in a light garlicky broth.
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the water and fish sauce, then bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the chicken is tender, then shred the meat.
Return the shredded chicken to the pot and add the noodles.
Simmer for 3 minutes, then top with chopped green onion before serving.

name: Beef Mami
description: Egg noodle soup with tender beef slices in a savory beef broth.
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the beef and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the water and fish sauce, then bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer for 30 minutes until the beef is tender, then slice thinly.
Return the beef to the pot and add the noodles.
Simmer for 3 minutes, then top with chopped green onion before serving.

name: Misua with Patola
description: Delicate wheat noodle soup with sponge gourd in a light garlicky broth.
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Pour in the water and fish sauce, then bring to a boil.
Add the sliced patola and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the misua noodles and simmer for 2 minutes until softened.
Serve hot immediately.

name: Misua with Meatballs
description: Delicate wheat noodle soup with small pork meatballs.
instructions: Season the ground pork with salt and shape into small meatballs.
Heat oil in a pot and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Pour in the water and fish sauce, then bring to a boil.
Drop in the meatballs and simmer for 8 minutes until cooked through.
Add the misua noodles and simmer for 2 minutes until softened, then serve.

name: Garlic Fried Rice
description: Day-old rice fried with plenty of toasted garlic until fragrant.
instructions: Mince the garlic finely.
Heat oil in a pan and fry the garlic until golden and crisp, reserving some for topping.
Add the rice and toss to coat with the garlic oil.
Season with salt and cook for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Top with the reserved crispy garlic before serving.

name: Java Rice
description: Turmeric-tinted fried rice with a savory garlic and onion base.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Stir in the turmeric powder and cook for 1 minute.
Add the rice and toss until evenly colored.
Season with soy sauce and cook for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Serve hot.

name: Adobo Fried Rice
description: Fried rice cooked in leftover adobo sauce with shredded pork.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and saute the garlic until golden.
Add the pork and cook until browned.
Pour in the soy sauce and vinegar, then simmer for 5 minutes until the pork is tender, then shred it.
Add the rice and toss until evenly coated in the adobo sauce.
Cook for 3 minutes more, then serve.

name: Tinapa Fried Rice
description: Smoky fried rice made with flaked smoked fish and garlic.
instructions: Flake the tinapa meat, removing any bones and skin.
Heat oil in a pan and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the flaked tinapa and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the rice and toss well to combine.
Season with salt and cook for 4 minutes, stirring often, then serve.

name: Yang Chow Fried Rice
description: Restaurant-style fried rice with shrimp, ham, egg, and green peas.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and saute the garlic until golden.
Push the garlic aside and scramble the eggs in the pan.
Add the shrimp and cook until pink.
Add the ham, carrot, and green peas, and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the rice and soy sauce, and toss until well combined.
Cook for 4 minutes more, stirring often, then serve.

name: Pork Fried Rice
description: Fried rice tossed with savory bits of pork and garlic.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the pork and cook until browned and cooked through.
Add the rice and soy sauce, and toss to combine.
Cook for 4 minutes more, stirring often, then serve.

name: Chicken Fried Rice
description: Fried rice tossed with savory bits of chicken and garlic.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook until browned and cooked through.
Add the rice and soy sauce, and toss to combine.
Cook for 4 minutes more, stirring often, then serve.

name: Beef Fried Rice
description: Fried rice tossed with savory bits of beef and garlic.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the beef and cook until browned.
Add the rice and soy sauce, and toss to combine.
Cook for 4 minutes more, stirring often, then serve.

name: Tofu Sisig
description: Crispy diced tofu sizzled with onions, chili, and a splash of calamansi.
instructions: Cut the tofu into small cubes and pat dry.
Heat oil in a pan and fry the tofu until golden and crisp, then drain.
In a separate pan with a little oil, saute the onion and chili.
Add the fried tofu, soy sauce, and pepper, and toss well.
Squeeze in calamansi juice just before serving.

name: Crispy Tofu
description: Golden fried tofu slices, crisp outside and soft inside.
instructions: Slice the tofu and pat dry with paper towels.
Season with salt and dust with cornstarch.
Heat oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Fry the tofu until golden and crisp on all sides.
Drain on paper towels and serve with a soy-vinegar dip.

name: Salt and Pepper Tofu
description: Crispy fried tofu tossed with garlic, bell pepper, salt, and pepper.
instructions: Cut the tofu into cubes, pat dry, and dust with cornstarch.
Heat oil in a pan and fry the tofu until golden and crisp, then drain.
In a separate pan with a little oil, saute the garlic and bell pepper.
Toss the fried tofu with the sauteed garlic, bell pepper, salt, and pepper.
Serve hot.

name: Adobong Tokwa
description: Fried tofu braised adobo-style in garlic, soy sauce, and vinegar.
instructions: Cut the tofu into cubes and fry in a little oil until golden, then set aside.
In the same pan, saute the garlic until fragrant.
Add the soy sauce, water, bay leaf, and peppercorns, then simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the vinegar and boil without stirring for 2 minutes.
Return the tofu to the pan and simmer for 3 minutes more, then serve.

name: Tokwa't Baboy
description: Fried tofu and boiled pork cubes tossed in a garlicky soy-vinegar sauce.
instructions: Boil the pork belly in water until tender, about 20 minutes, then dice.
Cut the tofu into cubes and fry in hot oil until golden, then drain.
Combine the soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, onion, and sugar in a bowl to make the sauce.
Toss the pork and tofu with the sauce.
Serve as a snack or side dish.

name: Tokwa at Sitaw
description: Fried tofu and string beans sauteed in a savory shrimp paste sauce.
instructions: Cut the tofu into cubes and fry in a little oil until golden, then set aside.
Heat oil in a pan and saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the pork and cook until browned.
Add the sitaw and water, then cover and simmer for 6 minutes.
Stir in the shrimp paste and fried tofu.
Cook for 3 minutes more, then serve.

name: Tokwa with Oyster Sauce
description: Crispy fried tofu tossed in a savory oyster sauce and garlic glaze.
instructions: Cut the tofu into cubes and fry in hot oil until golden, then drain.
In a separate pan, saute garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the oyster sauce and water, then simmer for 2 minutes.
Add the cornstarch slurry and cook until the sauce thickens.
Toss in the fried tofu and coat well before serving.

name: Braised Tofu with Mushrooms
description: Silken tofu and mushrooms braised together in a light savory sauce.
instructions: Cut the tofu into cubes.
